blocking.summary: installRenderCounters keeps the renderer.shadowMap and renderer.info objects it found at boot. three r180 initGLContext, which onContextRestore calls again (bundle: function _e(){... N() ...}, and N() sets v.shadowMap=Se and v.info=at), replaces both objects. After any WebGL context restore the shadow wrapper is never called and calls/tris are read from the dead WebGLInfo, so the ?qa readout is silently wrong.
blocking.reproduced: Forced loss and restore with WEBGL_lose_context (scripts/ctx-restore-repro.mjs; ctx-restore-chrome.json, ctx-restore-webkit.json): before, GL draws 2416 = 1206 + 1210; after, GL draws still 2416 but the readout gives shadowCalls 0, shadowTris 0, and shadowUpdates frozen (Chrome 48 while frames go 48 -> 105; WebKit 41 while frames go 41 -> 82). renderer.shadowMap and renderer.info are new objects (shadowMapReplaced true, infoReplaced true).
blocking.naturalOccurrence: WebKit 27.2, a V2 load that logged "WebGL: context lost." and recovered (q1-verify-webkit.json, B.V2): readout calls 1119, tris 126,642, shadowCalls 0, while the live renderer.info said 479 and the GL drew 1692 (= 479 + 1213). In the boot probe 4 of 15 WebKit loads per tree logged a context loss; 2 work loads (3 base) still reached ready, i.e. sessions in which the readout would be wrong without any sign.
blocking.impact: Q1 exists to give honest counters. In WebKit (a mandatory browser) the counters lie after a frequent, known event; Q1-a then fails and its WebKit retry hides the defect as the "known context loss"; Q2 gates read in WebKit (idle frames add 0 to shadowUpdates, main-pass calls) could pass on frozen values. The GPU timer has the same gap: pending queries from the lost context never resolve and the extension is not fetched again after a restore.
blocking.fix: Read renderer.info and renderer.shadowMap live; in countedRender wrap renderer.shadowMap.render again whenever renderer.shadowMap is not the wrapped object (or listen for webglcontextrestored on renderer.domElement); drop pending GPU queries and get the extension again on restore; expose a contextRestores count in the readout. Tests: a unit case with a fake renderer that swaps info and shadowMap, and a browser case in grab.spec that forces loseContext/restoreContext and checks calls = overlay and shadowCalls = census prediction afterwards.

nonBlocking: gpuMs is described as the GPU time of the main pass (LookDev.js:38, SMOKE_PROTOCOL, commit bodies, baseline V1 6.80 ms), but the query brackets the whole canvas render() call, and three runs shadowMap.render inside render(); the value is shadow pass + main pass. Rename or document it before Q2/Q6 use it.
